ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the perpendiculars to the x-axis and y-axis through the point $M(-3, 2)$ intersect the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{4}{x}$ at points A and B, respectively. What is the area of the quadrilateral MAOB?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure\\
Substitute $y=2$ into $y=\frac{4}{x}$ to find $x=2$\\
$\therefore B\left(2,2\right)$, $C\left(0,2\right)$\\
Substitute $x=-3$ into $y=\frac{4}{x}$ to find $y=-\frac{4}{3}$\\
$\therefore A\left(-3,-\frac{4}{3}\right)$, $D\left(-3,0\right)$\\
$\therefore {S}_{\text{quadrilateral }MAOB}={S}_{\triangle BOC}+{S}_{\triangle AOD}+{S}_{\text{rectangle }MDOC}$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}OC\times BC+\frac{1}{2}OD\times AD+OD\times OC$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 2+\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times \frac{4}{3}+3\times 2$\\
$=\boxed{10}$

A horizontal segment from M extends rightward to point B on the branch of the curve in quadrant I, and a vertical segment from M extends downward to point A on the branch of the curve in quadrant III.
